# the exact Dreamcast file that still owns its matching written procedure.

column5: Complete selection destructor Windows583bb8..583c35 and Mac17b5b0..17b6bc contain virtual resource/CSprite dispose operations without calls to the ordinary namespace wrappers. Source retains canonical ResourceManager::dispose calls across TU; shared-header visibility is required to permit both compilers to expand wrappers. DC source owner is older snapshot evidence; preserve body/declaration, record exact reviewed Mac+Windows ownership divergence. This is not WIN_ONLY because DC counterpart exists.

DC CodeView places playerData::IsHuman at game.cpp:1946 (dc 0xa6144). Complete retains Windows 0x4bada0 and Mac 0xcdbf0, while Windows hero::giveArtifact expands the query at 0x4e322d and Mac expands it at 0x103f74. Keeping the definition in the shared class header exposes one canonical body to these callers across TUs. This is a reviewed source-placement difference from the older DC snapshot, not a Windows-only helper.

The older Dreamcast line table attributes reset to Game.h. Complete retains its Windows body at 0x4bc350 and Mac body at code0+0xcf6f0, both called within game::save; placing the ordinary definition in game.cpp lets VC6 emit the retail body and preserves the canonical call without a cross-TU visibility requirement. A shared inline header definition suppresses both claimed Windows functions in the integrated build.
